description: One evolving workspace evaluated as a sequence of independent live snapshots. Each step must be built from that step's snapshot alone -- no step's expected result can be derived by reusing or caching a previous step's FrontResult. The story: B blocks its dependent A in the same batch, B's later close unblocks A, a freshly discovered async gate then re-poisons the whole front, the gate's resolution plus a reprioritized/relimited pool changes who is selected, and a failure that reopens the previously-dispatched top candidate must be picked up by the very next recomputation.

steps.description: Initial capture: B and its dependent A are both ready. B has not closed within this batch, so A must not unlock alongside it.

B has since closed and a fresh live poll no longer surfaces it as ready at all; A's blocking dependency is gone from this batch, and independent candidate C has also become ready. A must now be selected -- a stale reuse of the previous step's result would still show A excluded.

Same ready pool as the previous step (A, C), but a newly discovered async gate now targets A. Fresh recomputation must re-poison the whole front even though the immediately prior recomputation was clean.

Gate G is gone entirely from the live query (resolved and no longer reported), a new higher-priority candidate D has appeared, and the pool is now read with live_ready_order=false and a tighter cap. Recomputation must reflect the new priority ordering and cap, not the previous step's membership or order.

D was dispatched in the previous step but its run failed, so bd reopened it back to ready. Freed capacity now covers the whole pool. The very next recomputation must pick D back up rather than remembering it as already handled.
